problem_statement: Federated multi-label classification suffers from label co-occurrence heterogeneity: each client observes different local label relationships, so naive global aggregation can amplify local spurious correlations while ignoring reliable semantic or domain knowledge.
existing_weakness: A label graph should not be an extra branch or a posterior echo of the server prior. The framework must clearly separate inference-time graph-masked reasoning from upload-time data-only local graph extraction.
method_summary: FedGraphHarmony builds a confidence-aware prior label graph, uses it as a communication mask inside label-token attention, extracts local graph evidence from data-only attention scores, and personalizes federated aggregation with low-confidence structural residuals.
image_prompt_override:
Create one wide 16:9 camera-ready overview figure for a machine learning paper named FedGraphHarmony. Make it much more orderly and structured than a dense freeform diagram. Use a clean white background, thin black outlines, restrained colors, Times New Roman-like serif labels, no standalone title, no caption, no watermark.

Overall layout: use three horizontal swimlanes plus one right-side server column. The visual reading order must be obvious: left to right, then down, then right. Use numbered stage badges 1, 2, 3, 4. Keep arrows mostly straight or right-angled. Avoid crossing arrows. Avoid large A B C D panel letters. Keep all text short and inside boxes.

Stage 1, top swimlane, label '1 Prior graph'. Place it across the upper left to upper middle. Inputs: 'Label text E', 'Semantic edges', 'Knowledge edges'. These merge into two matrix icons labeled 'A0' and 'C0'. Then a small server output chip: 'Ag^t, Cg^t'. Use green color for prior knowledge. Show high-confidence edges as solid green and low-confidence uncertain edges as pale dashed lines.

Stage 2, middle main swimlane, label '2 Local reasoning'. This is the largest and most central lane. Use blue color for client computation. Show a simple left-to-right pipeline: 'Image tokens X' and 'Label queries E' feed into 'Label-query grounding', output 'Label tokens Z'. Then show 'Graph-masked label attention' as a large box. Inside it, show a data score matrix 'D' multiplied by graph mask 'Mg', then 'softmax', then updated label tokens 'H'. Put the small formula 'S = D x Mg' inside this box. Above the mask, show 'Mg from Ag^t, Cg^t'. Add a small loss chip below: 'BCE + weighted KL'. Keep this lane clean and aligned.

Stage 3, bottom swimlane, label '3 Data-only evidence'. It must be visually separated from Stage 2. From the unmasked data score D, draw a separate downward branch labeled 'bypass mask'. Show the sequence 'D' -> 'RowNorm' -> 'Sym' -> 'EMA' -> 'Ahat_l,k'. Add a small tag 'no prior echo'. Use pale blue color. This branch represents upload evidence only, not inference.

Stage 4, right-side server column, label '4 Server update'. Use amber color for personalization and green for global graph. Show stacked client uploads 'Ahat_l,1 ... Ahat_l,K' entering the server. Inside the server column, use two aligned rows: row one 'Global graph update' producing 'Ag^(t+1)'; row two 'Low-confidence residual' producing 'z_k' and 'S_kl'. Then split into two output boxes: 'FedAvg backbone theta' and 'Personalized relation psi_k'. Draw one clean return arrow from the server back to Stage 2 labeled 'next round'.

Add a small legend in the lower right corner, inside the server column or beside it. Legend items: solid green edge means high-confidence anchored; dashed pale edge means low-confidence adaptive; blue boxes mean client reasoning; amber boxes mean personalization. Keep the legend small.

Text discipline: no paragraphs, no sentences longer than five words, no repeated explanatory text, no misspellings. Specifically write 'Calculate residual vectors' correctly if that phrase appears, but prefer the shorter label 'Residual vectors'. Keep formulas short and readable. Do not use Greek letters if they make text illegible; use theta and psi as plain words if needed.

Important visual quality constraints: balanced margins, aligned columns, consistent box sizes, consistent arrow thickness, enough whitespace between modules, no overlapping labels, no tangled long curved arrows, no bottom-wide caption strip, no giant decorative icons. The final image should look like a polished, orderly NeurIPS/ICLR method overview figure.
